statement_scope: Let J be the original family of nondegenerate closed intervals in R and A its exact set of centers. For every x in A and epsilon>0 there exists I in J centered at x with 0<|I|<epsilon; retain D=sup_{I in J}|I|<infinity. Under the author-explicit A subset (0,1), there exist two at-most-countable subfamilies F1,F2 of {I in J:I subset (0,1)}, each pairwise disjoint as closed sets, with A subset (union F1) union (union F2). No A measurability/compactness, a.e. loss, dilation or cross-family disjointness asserted.
